subject: Allocation of Indemnity Across MSA + Order Forms — proposed waterfall
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, contracts@cyphersys.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed allocation approach for CypherSys redlines (MSA + multi-OF)

Team —

CypherSys sent their redline this morning; principal tension is how indemnity stacks between the MSA and multiple order forms (they expect per-OF caps to be additive to the MSA cap). They also want defense-cost sharing on any claim tied to customer inputs.

My proposal (to send as our counter) is: a waterfall approach where the MSA remains the umbrella obligation (defend & indemnify for core product IP only), and each Order Form can add narrow, product-specific indemnities but cannot increase the aggregate cap beyond the MSA cap unless explicitly negotiated with procurement (i.e., no automatic stacking). For third-party claims tied to customer content, require notice + opportunity to control defense, and a 30/70 cost-split only if the claim clearly arises from customer's proprietary materials — otherwise we defend.

Questions for legal/procurement:
- Kimberly: is the waterfall language defensible and reasonable to present (I attached a draft snippet)?
- Ben: if we keep aggregate cap, do we need a commercial concession (credit/fee) to compensate CypherSys?
- Laura: if we accept defense-first but with cost-split backstop, who is the litigation liaison and do we pre-authorize outside counsel limits?

I've attached my redline of section 8 (indemnity + caps) and an evidence_matrix template we can ask them to fill if they push for quicker notice windows.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_rdw_msa_v3.pdf, evidence_matrix.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed allocation approach for CypherSys redlines (MSA + multi-OF)

Irene — good framing. A few legal notes inline and high-level:

1) Waterfall approach: defensible and customer-friendly. Draft language should (a) identify the MSA as the governing umbrella, (b) prevent per-OF stacking by specifying that OF caps "flow up" into the MSA cap unless an amendment expressly increases aggregate liability.

2) Defense control: push for "right to assume defense" with standard cooperation and insurance-first preference. Avoid language that allows automatic recovery from customer inputs without a clear evidentiary threshold.

3) Evidence/notice window: we should keep a 60-day cure/notice period for non-IP claims, 30 days for IP notices is aggressive from our side — propose a compromise of 45 days for actionable evidence to be lodged.

4) Escrow/evidence package: the evidence_matrix we request should be limited (claims summary, reproducer, third-party notices). We should NOT accept broad discovery obligations in the MSA.

Attaching my redline (redline_rdw_msa_v3.pdf) with suggested language and a short comment thread to include with our counter. If procurement wants to offer any credit to CypherSys for non-stacking, can we record that as a one-time onboarding credit rather than increase recurring fees?

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_rdw_msa_v3.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed allocation approach for CypherSys redlines (MSA + multi-OF)

Agree with Kimberly on the legal framing. A couple procurement points:

- We cannot accept any language that effectively caps us higher on a per-OF basis without commercial consideration. If we keep the aggregate cap in the MSA, CypherSys will push for a concession — recommend a one-time onboarding credit (USD 25k) or a 5% fee reduction on year-1 billings in exchange for no stacking.

- Escrow / insurance-first: prefer a carrier-first waterfall (i.e., require claimant to exhaust insurer coverage before drawing on vendor). That reduces our direct cash exposure.

- Notice timing: 45 days from our perspective is okay. However, for operational SLAs we should keep a 14-day acknowledgement SLA and 30-day remediation window for evidence handover. The evidence_matrix.xlsx should include fields we can validate (timestamped logs, sample payloads).

If legal is comfortable with the redline, I'm happy to greenlight the commercial concession and have Laura lock in the signature delegation (I can only approve credits up to 30k; anything above needs VP sign-off).

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts (Procurement Lead)
Redwood Inference

From: Amir Patel <amir@cyphersys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, contracts@cyphersys.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Allocation of Indemnity Across MSA + Order Forms — CypherSys counter

Hi Irene / team —

Thanks for the clear note. We want to be pragmatic:

- We can accept a waterfall umbrella, but need a clear guardrail that an OF may include additional indemnity for discrete modules (e.g., a fine-tuning offering). We propose that per-OF indemnities are allowed only if expressly listed and the OF states the additional cap; otherwise they do not stack.

- For third-party claims tied to customer inputs, we are willing to accept notice/cooperation and a right to assume defense, but request a 50/50 defense-cost split if the claim arises from the customer's data or prompts (we will not accept full liability in those cases).

- On caps: we cannot accept a unilateral aggregate reduction. If Redwood insists on a single aggregate cap, we require a modest onboarding credit (USD 20k) or a 4% reduction in year-1 fees.

I've attached our counter redline and a short OF example to show how we think additional OF-specific indemnities should be invoked (cyphersys_orderform_counter_v2.docx). Happy to jump on a 30-minute call next week to walk through.

Best,
Amir Patel
General Counsel, CypherSys
Attachments: cyphersys_orderform_counter_v2.docx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-03T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Allocation of Indemnity Across MSA + Order Forms — final next steps

Amir / team — appreciate the quick turn. Summary of agreed points for internal signoff:

1) Waterfall accepted in principle: MSA umbrella with permitted per-OF incremental indemnities only when explicitly listed (no automatic stacking).
2) Defense: Redwood retains right to assume defense with cooperation obligations. For customer-input claims, we accept a 50/50 cost-split only where evidence clearly shows customer origin; otherwise Redwood defends.
3) Notice & evidence windows: agree to 45-day actionable notice; operational acknowledgment within 14 days and evidence packet within 30 days of acknowledgement.
4) Commercial concession: tentative agreement on a one-time onboarding credit; procurement to confirm exact amount (Ben: propose 20–25k).
5) Escrow/evidence: CypherSys to complete the evidence_matrix template if they want accelerated handling.

Next steps:
- Legal to finalize the redline (Kimberly & Irene) and circulate to CypherSys by EOD Thursday.
- Procurement (Ben & Laura) to confirm the exact onboarding credit and signatory delegation (Irene: please specify who can execute DocuSign).
- Schedule a 30-minute alignment call early next week; I'll propose times after legal redline is ready.

For signature delegation: Laura, can we pre-authorize your team to sign up to USD 30k credit? If yes, please confirm and we'll route the DocuSign envelope (link below).
